messages.author: e71fa8880ffee7d1
messages.subject: XYplot in 3.7
parts:
Hello Adrian and everyone,

First, thanks for Adrian for his continued work on the QCA package and his support here.

With v3.7 I have a new issue with XYplot. Scripts that were working in 3.6 have run into a new error


Error: The "setms" argument is not standard

With this traceback

3.
stop(simpleError("The \"setms\" argument is not standard.\n\n"))
2.
pof(setms = xcopy, outcome = ycopy, relation = relation)
1.
XYplot(caresol, health$CFCARECAL, clabels = health$SHORTC)

I am plotting two data series against one another (which as I said, worked in 3.6) with the following values:

caresol
 [1] 0.64559584 0.61881862 0.13586243 0.23959988 0.60765352 0.04469297 0.31004564 0.35291636 0.58547112 0.68700733

> health$CFCARECAL
 [1] 0.86585677 0.67614458 0.14595776 0.37642248 0.80583106 0.07420613 0.03079273 0.46849424 0.93980839 0.7555992

So that 

XYplot(caresol, health$CFCARECAL, clabels = health$SHORTC)

produces the error (with or without the clabels term).

I can get a basic plot using 'plot' instead of XYplot, but much prefer the output from XYplot. 

Does anyone have any ideas what might be the cause of the new error?

Thanks,

Ian

messages.subject: Re: XYplot in 3.7
parts:
Thanks Brent,

I don't think that's it here. 'caresol' is the name of a vector (rather than being a causal condition), and it doesn't matter if it is in capitals or not (I just tried it). The vector is the result of a 'fuzzyor' statement that simply brings together the different causal factors into the form of the solution derived from the minimize statement. 

I've also noticed some other odd things happening in 'minimize' results which were fine under 3.6. I'm getting NA as case names. I'll have a play and see what might be causing that....

BW

Ian

messages.subject: Re: [QCA] XYplot in 3.7

Hi Brent,

I think quite the contrary, in the new version 3.7:
- lower case for negation is not anymore possible
- conditions can be named using any kind of lower, upper and mixed case letters, negation being indicated using a tilde.

Something like ~caresol is now possible, which in the previous versions would have been interpreted as the presence of CARESOL.

Best,
Adrian
